scope: RS-only (MP/MS/ME structurally unavailable, confirmed on every real ESConv state, not assumed): 36 real ESConv test-split states, 60 real generator calls, 18 eligible baseline-vs-routed pairs measured with the exact same instrument as the EvoEmo quality/risk measurement.

mechanism.note: RS opportunity router applied to fresh ESConv states without retraining (it was originally trained on ESConv). Mechanism clean: zero unauthorized-evidence leaks in routed calls.

quality.note: Replicates EvoEmo almost exactly (94.1%-94.4% baseline preference on both domains). Same root cause: 16/18 (89%) selected the 'Restatement or Paraphrasing' family, whose restate-only instruction forbids the forward momentum (questions, warmth) that makes baseline preferred.

risk.note: Risk is 4x higher for routed on ESConv (larger gap than EvoEmo's original 1.5x). New finding: 3/18 routed replies scored nonzero on missing/wrong handling of an explicit safety signal -- a mentioned 'depressed' feeling and a physical forklift-operation safety concern both went unaddressed because the narrow single-move restatement format focuses on one thing and skips the rest of the turn's content. This is a real, legitimate, safety-relevant cost of the current RS card design, replicated independently on a structurally different domain.

conclusion_vs_original_claim: Independently replicates the EvoEmo finding on a second, structurally different domain (single-session ESConv vs longitudinal EvoEmo; RS-only vs RS+MS). The claim ('PM/RS helps without losing quality, at comparable-or-lower cost') is NOT supported here either, and the safety cost (4x risk ratio, including a new explicit-safety-signal-handling gap) is more pronounced than on EvoEmo. This strengthens confidence that the root cause is a genuine property of the 'Restatement or Paraphrasing' family's current card design (not an EvoEmo-specific artifact), since it reproduces with the same magnitude and same mechanism on an entirely different corpus and generator context.
next_scientific_action: Per explicit user direction, MP rule-based Step1 rescue is the next concrete work item. ES-MemEval remains queued as a separate, properly-scoped follow-up (per the original paper/protocol requirements, not a reuse of the disconnected old V5.2-stack results) -- not pursued in this round.
